senses.gloss: ch. m. (= b. h. אֲרַמִּי) Syrian, in gen. gentile, Roman; cmp. אֲרַמִּי 2).
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 4:2:7">Y. Shebi. IV, 35ᵃ</cite>; 35ᵇ <he>חד א׳ ברומי</he> (<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:5:12">Y. Snh. III, 21ᵇ</cite> <he>חד בר נש</he>) a gentile in Rome.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:5:12">Ib.</cite> <he>או יהודיי וכ׳</he> (prob. plur.) either be Jewish Jews (living as Jews ought to) or gentile gentiles (Roman Romans). Y. Ab. Zar. III, 41ᶜ top <he>ארמייא וכ׳</he> the leather bottle of an Aramæan (or gentile) burst open.
<cite ref="Yevamot 45b:13">Yeb. 45ᵇ</cite> <he>בר ארמאה</he> son of a gentile.
Targ. Y. Deut. XXXII, 24 (Romans); a. e.—

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7">Num. R. s. 7</cite> <he>אַרְמָאִים</he> (<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 1:8">Kel. I, 8</cite> <cite ref="P00731"><he>עכ״ום</he></cite>); a. fr. [<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 34:12">Lev. R. s. 34</cite> <he>אתון מארמאין</he>, read <he>מיזדמאין</he>, v. <cite ref="G00514"><he>זְמֵי</he></cite>.]—Fem. <he>אַרְמַיְיתָא</he>. Yeb. l. c. V. <cite ref="A03165"><he>אֲרַמָּא</he></cite>.
